question: In the TORCH screening acronym used during antenatal care, what does the letter 'R' stand for?
explanation: The letter R stands for Rubella. It is a viral infection that can lead to serious birth defects if caught during early pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why can TORCH infections be tricky to spot in pregnant women just by looking at them?

options.A: Physical signs only appear after delivery occurs
options.B: Maternal blood pressure hides any signs of infection
options.C: Mothers often show no symptoms or only mild, flu-like signs
options.D: Symptoms are completely hidden by normal pregnancy discomforts

explanation: Many pregnant women experience either no symptoms at all or very mild illness, which is why routine lab screening during antenatal care is so important. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h1)

question: How do pregnant women most commonly catch Toxoplasmosis?

options.A: Being bitten by infected mosquitoes during the rainy season
options.B: Eating undercooked meat and handling contaminated cat feces
options.C: Drinking unpasteurized cow milk and swimming in stagnant water
options.D: Inhaling droplets from an infected person's sneeze

explanation: Toxoplasma parasites are frequently found in raw or undercooked meat, as well as in soil or cat litter handled without washing hands. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which infant condition is classically linked to a congenital toxoplasmosis infection?

options.A: Complete absence of heart valves at birth
options.B: Enlarged kidneys with multiple fluid cysts
options.D: Severe bone fractures of the lower limbs

explanation: When this parasite infects the developing fetal brain, it can cause fluid accumulation and characteristic calcium deposits. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h2)

question: What are the three classic birth defects that make up congenital rubella syndrome?

options.A: Skin rash, joint pain, and kidney failure

explanation: An infant born with congenital rubella frequently presents with eye cataracts, hearing loss, and heart anomalies. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h3)

question: A woman with active genital herpes lesions is admitted in labor at 39 weeks. What is the standard management to protect the newborn?

options.A: Induce labor quickly with oxytocin to shorten the second stage
options.B: Delay delivery with drugs until the lesions disappear
options.C: Perform a planned cesarean section before membranes rupture
options.D: Give oral antibiotics immediately and encourage normal delivery

explanation: A cesarean section prevents the newborn from coming into direct contact with active herpes lesions in the birth canal. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h3)

question: Why does a maternal infection in the first trimester usually cause more severe structural defects than one in the third trimester?

options.A: Major fetal organs and body structures are actively forming during the first trimester
options.B: The placenta is completely absent during the first three months
options.C: Pathogens multiply much faster in amniotic fluid during early gestation
options.D: Maternal immune defenses are completely shut down in early pregnancy

explanation: Because major organs develop early in pregnancy, tissues are especially vulnerable to disruption by infections during the first trimester. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign of a congenital TORCH infection in a newborn?

options.A: Marked macrosomia and excessive birth weight
options.D: Small spots of bleeding under the skin from low platelets

explanation: TORCH infections typically lead to growth restriction rather than excess weight gain, alongside signs like liver enlargement and bruising. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h4)

question: What does the presence of specific IgM antibodies in a pregnant woman's blood test usually indicate?

options.A: Complete absence of any immune response
options.C: A recent or fresh primary infection
options.D: A chronic infection acquired years ago

explanation: IgM antibodies are the first ones the immune system produces during a new infection, pointing to recent exposure. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h5)

question: Which test is commonly used to confirm an infection in the baby when a pregnant woman's screening is positive?

options.A: Routine external abdominal palpation and fundal height measurement
options.B: Continuous electronic fetal heart rate monitoring
options.C: Amniocentesis for polymerase chain reaction testing
options.D: A baseline biophysical profile ultrasound scan

explanation: Testing a sample of amniotic fluid via PCR detects pathogen DNA directly, showing whether the infection has crossed to the baby. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h5)

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment when a pregnant woman contracts toxoplasmosis?

options.A: To reduce the risk of the infection crossing the placenta to the baby
options.B: To speed up the onset of labor and delivery
options.C: To dissolve existing calcium deposits in the baby's brain
options.D: To completely turn off the mother's normal immune response

explanation: Antiparasitic treatment during pregnancy helps lower the chances of the parasite passing through to the baby's circulation. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the standard approach for managing a maternal Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection during pregnancy?

options.A: Supportive care and regular ultrasound scans to check fetal growth
options.B: Immediate high-dose antiviral pills to cure the mother
options.C: Emergency termination of pregnancy in all confirmed cases
options.D: Weekly blood transfusions to prevent severe maternal anemia

explanation: Since there is no definitive cure for CMV during pregnancy, care focuses on monitoring the baby's well-being and managing symptoms. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h6)

question: Why is the Rubella vaccine never given to women who are currently pregnant?

options.A: It triggers immediate premature rupture of the membranes
options.B: It is completely ineffective during pregnancy
options.C: It causes severe allergic reactions in all pregnant women
options.D: It is a live vaccine that could potentially harm the developing baby

explanation: Rubella is a live-attenuated vaccine, so it is withheld during pregnancy and given safely after delivery if the mother lacks immunity. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h7)

question: A first-time pregnant mother asks how to prevent toxoplasmosis at home. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Wear a face mask whenever leaving the house in the afternoon
options.B: Take daily antibiotics throughout the entire pregnancy
options.C: Cook all meat thoroughly and wash hands after handling soil or raw food
options.D: Avoid eating fresh green vegetables and citrus fruits completely

explanation: Good food hygiene, thoroughly cooked meat, and washing hands after handling soil or raw food are the best ways to prevent toxoplasmosis. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h7)
